matchstick.title: Check arithmetic validity
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, compute the numeric values of both sides of the equation and verify they are equal. A visually correct equation can still be mathematically false, so arithmetic verification is essential.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever you propose a stick move that changes any numeral or operator.
matchstick.example: Resulting equation looks syntactically correct but does not satisfy the arithmetic (e.g., 12 = 1).

matchstick.title: Preserve valid numeral shapes
matchstick.principle: When a stick is removed from or added to a Roman numeral, the resulting shape must correspond to a recognized numeral (I, V, X, L, C, D, M). A single diagonal or an incomplete shape is not a valid numeral.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever the move involves a numeral.
matchstick.example: Removing a diagonal stick from an X, leaving a single diagonal line, which is not a valid Roman numeral.

matchstick.title: Operator stick composition
matchstick.principle: Know the exact sticks that make up each operator: '+' = one vertical + one horizontal; '-' = one horizontal; '=' = two horizontals. Any transformation must respect these compositions.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When changing an operator or moving a stick to/from an operator.
matchstick.example: Turning '+' into '=' by removing its vertical stick without adding a horizontal stick, leaving an invalid operator.

matchstick.title: Allowed operators only
matchstick.principle: The only operators permitted are '+', '-', and '=', and the equality sign may not be turned into '≠' or any other symbol. Ensure the final equation uses only these operators.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Throughout the solution, especially when modifying operators.
matchstick.example: Changing the equality sign into '≠' or any other symbol not among '+', '-', '='.

matchstick.title: Match‑stick orientation matters
matchstick.principle: When converting one operator to another, the stick you move must have the correct orientation (vertical or horizontal) required by the target operator. A vertical stick cannot replace a missing horizontal, and vice‑versa.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to add or remove a stick to change an operator.
matchstick.example: Adding a vertical stick to a '-' to make '+' without having a vertical stick available from another character.

matchstick.title: Do not break X or V
matchstick.principle: X and V consist of two diagonal sticks; removing one leaves an invalid shape. Avoid moving a stick from X or V unless you can simultaneously create another valid numeral with the removed stick.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When considering moving a stick from a numeral that is X or V.
matchstick.example: Taking a stick from a V, leaving a single diagonal line, which is not a valid numeral.

matchstick.title: Operator‑to‑operator moves
matchstick.principle: A useful strategy is to relocate a stick from one operator to another (e.g., from '=' to '+') to create a second '=' sign, forming a chain of equalities that can satisfy the equation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains both an equality sign and another operator.
matchstick.example: Ignoring the possibility of moving a stick from one operator to another to create a chain of equalities.

matchstick.title: Limit changes to two characters
matchstick.principle: Moving a single stick can only affect the source character (which loses a stick) and the destination character (which gains a stick). All other characters must remain unchanged.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When planning the move, ensure you do not alter more than two symbols.
matchstick.example: Altering more than two characters (e.g., changing several numerals) when only one stick should be moved.

matchstick.title: Maintain a valid equality
matchstick.principle: The final equation must contain exactly one equality sign (or a chain of equalities) and only allowed operators. Do not drop the equality sign or replace it with an invalid operator.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After the move, before finalizing the answer.
matchstick.example: Producing an equation without an equality sign or with multiple operators that break the allowed set (e.g., 'X + II + I').

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on visual shape changes and neglects the underlying numeric evaluation.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always compute the values of both sides after the move and confirm they match.

matchstick.why_it_happens: Misinterpretation of the rule that '=' cannot become '≠' or any other symbol.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Recall the allowed operator set (+, -, =) and never introduce other symbols.

matchstick.why_it_happens: Assumes any removal or addition of a stick yields a valid Roman numeral.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Check the resulting shape against the list of valid Roman numeral glyphs before finalizing the move.

matchstick.why_it_happens: Lack of explicit knowledge of which sticks form each operator.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Memorize the stick composition of '+', '-', and '=' and ensure transformations respect it.

matchstick.description: Moving sticks from X or V
matchstick.why_it_happens: Assumes any stick can be removed without affecting the validity of the numeral.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Recognize that X and V require both diagonal sticks; avoid removing a stick from them unless you can repurpose it to form another valid numeral.
